definitions.explanation: The most common variety of cherry blossom tree in Japan (Prunus × yedoensis). Produces pale pink to white flowers and accounts for roughly 80% of cherry trees in Japan.

examples.japanese: {染井吉野|そめいよしの}が{満開|まんかい}だ。
examples.english: The Somei-Yoshino cherries are in full bloom.

examples.japanese: {桜|さくら}の{開花|かいか}{予想|よそう}は{染井吉野|そめいよしの}を{基準|きじゅん}にしている。
examples.english: Cherry blossom forecasts are based on Somei-Yoshino trees.

examples.japanese: {染井吉野|そめいよしの}は{江戸時代|えどじだい}{末期|まっき}に{東京|とうきょう}の{染井村|そめいむら}で{生|う}まれた{品種|ひんしゅ}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Somei-Yoshino is said to be a variety that originated in Somei village in Tokyo in the late Edo period.

notes:
NAME ORIGIN:
{染井|そめい} refers to {染井村|そめいむら}, a village in what is now {豊島区|としまく}{駒込|こまごめ}, {東京|とうきょう}. {吉野|よしの} refers to {吉野山|よしのやま} in {奈良県|ならけん}, historically famous for cherry blossoms. The variety was bred by nurseries in {染井村|そめいむら} and named after both locations.

CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE:
{染井吉野|そめいよしの} is the standard reference tree for Japan's {桜|さくら}{開花|かいか}{予想|よそう} (cherry blossom forecast). When news reports say "the cherry blossoms have bloomed," they mean {染井吉野|そめいよしの} specifically. All trees of this variety are clones propagated by grafting, so they bloom almost simultaneously in any given area.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {染井吉野|そめいよしの}の{並木|なみき}: row of Somei-Yoshino trees
- {染井吉野|そめいよしの}が{咲|さ}く: Somei-Yoshino blooms
- {染井吉野|そめいよしの}の{開花|かいか}: blooming of Somei-Yoshino
